stories.Headline: Asian shares tumble, oil rises as markets await AI sector results
stories.Summary:
Asian stocks fell broadly on Oct 20, 2026, as investors waited for results from artificial intelligence companies. The MSCI Asia ex-Japan index dropped 1.14 percent, Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.98 percent and South Korea's KOSPI tumbled 3.92 percent, according to The Straits Times. Oil prices rose as markets weighed an executive order from US President Donald Trump that waived some sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy. Brent rose to US$109.64 per barrel and US crude rose to US$103.85 a barrel. The euro recouped some losses from the previous session after riots in France.

Quarterly earnings were due from SpaceX and Netflix on Oct 20, with Meta results expected on Wednesday and Tesla and chipmakers Lam Research and Texas Instruments later in the week, The Jakarta Post reported. Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers expected to increase combined capital expenditure to about US$1.2 trillion in 2027, according to Goldman Sachs. Shares in South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice Group plunged nearly 30 percent below their initial public offering price in their market debut, after the firm raised 201.1 billion won. Trump's executive order, issued on the night of Oct 16, waived key Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas, but Trump said on Oct 17 that he has yet to announce a final decision.

Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone, said in a note that the market is happy to cover shorts and unwind defensive trades, but that is very different from having the conviction to rebuild aggressive exposure to AI. He said French sovereign risk is clearly being priced into European equities, but the euro's resilience suggests traders are not yet treating it as a systemic European problem. Ninghui Liu, head of investment strategy and research for APAC at State Street Investment Management, said investors are fine with AI being used more, but they are questioning whether every dollar of AI capital expenditure earns more than it costs to finance. Daniel Morris, chief market strategist for AXA IM Core Investments at BNP Paribas Asset Management, said expectations are high because technology hardware dominates earnings growth, with the sector globally forecast to see a doubling of earnings compared with the same quarter a year ago.

French authorities set curfews in parts of several cities including Paris, Lille and Nice after a weekend of riots and looting stemming from nationwide anti-government protests. In the Middle East, dozens were killed and more than 200 were injured after an attack by the Iran-aligned Houthis on a government security forces training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province. Recent comments from Federal Reserve officials, including Chair Kevin Warsh, suggest policymakers are in no rush to hike rates again. European Central Bank policymaker Martin Kocher and Finnish central bank governor Olli Rehn were due to speak later on Oct 20, and Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee member Megan Greene was to deliver a speech at the London School of Economics. The US Census Bureau was due to release September figures, with housing starts expected to rise to 1.305 million from 1.275 million in August.

stories.Headline: Teradata adds privacy & resiliency for enterprise AI
stories.Summary:
Teradata announced new privacy, security and resiliency capabilities for enterprise AI data protection on October 20, 2026, according to a press release dated San Diego. The company said the additions cover data privacy, access controls and recovery measures across its cloud data platform. They are aimed at organisations that want to protect sensitive information used in AI systems while keeping critical operations available and recoverable if systems are disrupted. The launch includes Poly-Anonymization, which replaces personally identifiable information fields with stable identifiers, and format-preserving encryption, which protects sensitive values without changing their structure in downstream systems.

The update also adds post-quantum protections for data in transit through TLS 1.3 hybrid-key exchange, immutable backup protection, and database-level high availability based on real-time replication. The privacy functions come through an OEM partnership with Anonomatic, whose PII Vault stores underlying identity data separately from the analytical environment, so authorised users can restore identity when needed while others work with data that keeps its analytical relationships. Teradata also expanded policy-based access management through a partnership with Immuta, adding dynamic attribute-based access control so policies apply consistently across users and AI workloads without rewriting governance rules or duplicating datasets. Native features include dynamic data masking, data classification and tagging, column-level encryption, and a global identity framework. Teradata said internal testing at large scale showed multi-table join queries on protected data used fewer Teradata resources than equivalent queries on unprotected data, though results would vary by workload and configuration.

Sumeet Arora, Chief Product Officer at Teradata, said privacy, security and resiliency had historically been treated as separate problems with separate solutions, and that this approach does not hold up when AI moves sensitive data across users, applications, models and agents at the same time. He said the announcement reflects how the company thinks those capabilities need to work together and is the foundation for extending that protection as AI environments grow more complex and the actors within them multiply. Matt Fleck, Founder and CEO at Anonomatic, said enterprise AI creates a fundamentally different privacy challenge, because organisations need sensitive, individual-level data to build effective AI but traditional tools were not designed to preserve what AI needs. He said the partnership makes it possible to reduce identity exposure at enterprise scale without forcing organisations to choose between protection and utility.

Teradata argues that AI is changing enterprise data protection because sensitive information increasingly moves across users, applications, models and software agents, which makes perimeter-based security less effective on its own and raises the risk that non-identifiable data could be re-identified when AI combines multiple datasets. The company said its resiliency approach, called Enterprise Data Protection, matches protection levels to the criticality of specific workloads rather than applying the same architecture to every system, and aims to restore not only data after an incident but also the business context and operational information AI systems rely on. Privacy capabilities powered by Anonomatic are available now for Teradata Cloud on AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. Native data security features are available on those clouds, with dynamic data masking, data classification and tagging also offered for Teradata Factory and on-premises deployments. Immutable backup protection is available now on Teradata Cloud across the three hyperscale platforms, with availability on Teradata Customer Cloud planned in the coming months.

stories.Headline: How governments around the world are shaping what AI can say about politics
stories.Summary:
With the U.S. midterms approaching, about one in five voters has asked AI chatbots about elections and politics, a recent survey found. But many voters may not know that governments around the world increasingly shape what chatbots can say. Because many tech companies apply the same policies worldwide, the answers American voters get may be shaped by governments at home and abroad. A researcher at a nonpartisan think tank at Vanderbilt University, who studies free speech policy, worked with global legal experts on two reports published in 2025 and 2026. The reports examined how governments in 12 countries and regions regulate artificial intelligence, and found that they often use existing rules, such as national security or anti-state propaganda laws, rather than new AI laws to control what AI models can say.

In 2024, an Indian journalist asked Google's Gemini chatbot whether the policies of India's prime minister, Narendra Modi, were fascist, and Gemini responded that some experts say yes. The government reacted by requiring official permission before unreliable AI models could be released, though authorities later dropped this requirement. China requires AI models to uphold socialist core values, and in Turkey a court blocked posts by Grok, the chatbot built into X, that allegedly insulted President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, founding father Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and religious values. Research by Turkish law scholar Yaman Akdeniz identifies the Turkish rulings as among the earliest documented cases of state censorship of chatbots. A Vietnamese court sentenced two activists who live in Germany to 17 years each in prison in December 2025 for spreading anti-state material, and prosecutors accused them of using AI to fake voices and images of Vietnamese leaders.

The European Union's AI Act, adopted in 2024, requires any company offering AI tools in Europe, wherever it is based, to mark AI-generated content, and Anthropic applies the marks globally because it has no reliable way to apply them by region. In August 2026, the EU placed ChatGPT under the strictest tier of its Digital Services Act, so OpenAI must now assess and reduce the systemic risks of its service, including risks to elections such as the spread of disinformation. The Dutch Data Protection Authority tested four chatbots before the 2025 national election and found that the political middle ground virtually disappears in their voting advice, and it urged providers to prevent their systems from being used for voting advice. In 2024, Thierry Breton, then the EU's top digital rules enforcer, reminded Elon Musk of his legal obligations before Musk's live interview with then-presidential candidate Donald Trump on X, warning against the spread of harmful content.

In 2025, President Trump issued an executive order on Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government, which requires the AI models the government buys to be truth-seeking, ideologically neutral and not favoring ideas such as diversity, equity and inclusion. The article says truth-seeking may sound like an objective, neutral term, but it can mean very different things to different people, and it notes that the president recently banned three news outlets from the White House for reporting what he called fiction and lies and dismissed media polls as fake. The Federal Trade Commission has suggested that AI companies that steer answers toward undisclosed ideological or biased objectives might break consumer protection law, and a 2025 Pew Research Center survey found that eight in 10 Americans believe Republican and Democratic voters cannot agree on basic facts. Dozens of states have passed laws restricting AI-generated political deepfakes, and California and Hawaii are two states that have banned sharing deceptive AI content about candidates in the months around an election, but U.S. courts have blocked both of those laws, citing the First Amendment. The article advises voters to treat a chatbot's answer as a starting point, to keep in mind that governments both foreign and domestic may try to influence the answer, and says AI responses should not replace critical thinking at the ballot box.

stories.Headline: Singapore Prime Minister attends high-level dialogue on AI, energy in Abu Dhabi
stories.Summary:
Lawrence Wong, Prime Minister of Singapore, attended a high-level bilateral business dialogue at Zayed National Museum in Abu Dhabi on 21st October 2026. The event was hosted by Khaldoon Khalifa Al Mubarak, Chairman of the Executive Affairs Authority, as part of Wong's official visit to the UAE. It brought together senior officials from both countries to explore cooperation in artificial intelligence, advanced technology and energy. The engagement was also attended by Saeed Al Hajeri, Minister of State, Dr Abdulnasser AlShaali, UAE Ambassador to Singapore, and Kamal R. Vaswani, Singapore's Ambassador to the UAE, along with other officials.

The dialogue built on the Comprehensive Partnership between the UAE and Singapore, signed in 2019. Companies including G42, Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, EDGE Group, ADNOC, Masdar and Emirates Nuclear Energy Company presented their projects. G42 showcased its full-stack AI offering, including the UAE-US AI Campus under construction, while MBZUAI highlighted its open foundation models and a recent executive education programme with NUS Business School. ADNOC is Singapore's largest supplier of crude oil, and Masdar discussed cross-border clean energy supply, while ENEC explored civil nuclear cooperation focused on human capacity development and knowledge sharing.

Wong said he had good discussions with leaders of major Emirati companies in energy, AI and advanced technologies. He said the talks explored strengthening energy security, diversifying supply chains and building resilience against future disruptions. He added that the UAE is an important investment destination for Singapore in the Middle East and that there is scope to deepen cooperation and help businesses tap opportunities across Southeast Asia and the Gulf. Khaldoon said the two countries have built a strong and longstanding partnership grounded in shared priorities and innovation, and that the discussions highlighted practical cooperation supporting energy security and long-term growth.

Separately, Emirati and French companies signed agreements on 20th October 2026 to expand cooperation in energy, AI and advanced technology. The deals were signed during the UAE-France Business Dialogue at Qasr Al Watan in Abu Dhabi, attended by French President Emmanuel Macron and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. MBZUAI, G42 and Analog signed three memorandums of understanding with AMI Labs on research and development, cloud computing and AI models, and robotics. ADNOC Gas signed an MoU with Schneider Electric, and ADNOC Refining signed two contracts with Technip Energies for refining capacity expansion and sustainable aviation fuel. Macron began a Gulf tour on Monday with stops in Kuwait, the UAE, Bahrain and Qatar, aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies, strengthening economic and defense ties, and supporting efforts to restore freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.Headline: A ‘kill switch’ is the wrong way to regulate AI. Here’s why
stories.Summary:
After high-profile hacking incidents involving advanced artificial intelligence agents, some politicians and business executives called for an AI kill switch, a safeguard that could shut down AI systems in an emergency. The idea is that if a model behaved in dangerous ways, humans could regain control by metaphorically flipping a switch from on to off. Several efforts at AI regulation in 2026 focused on the notion of a kill switch, including proposed congressional legislation such as the AI Kill Switch Act and California Gov. Gavin Newsom's executive order aimed at reining in AI. President Donald Trump opposed the idea as unnecessary regulation, and to date there has been no national regulation that includes a kill switch.

The articles say the kill switch metaphor has two problems as a national safeguard. First, it makes the global infrastructure supporting AI appear centralized, when in reality it is a web of interconnected technologies spread across the globe, and advanced models from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic rely on multiple computers and data centers spread out nationally. Second, the idea hides the human decision-making involved in training and deployment of frontier models, positioning humans outside the loop rather than as part of training, supervision and approval. In accounts of how OpenAI's model went rogue and hacked AI company Hugging Face, the AI agents were depicted as operating on their own agenda, but experts explained that OpenAI personnel turned off safety mechanisms, gave the model impossible tasks and left a door open to the internet.

Dylan Baker, a research engineer at the nonprofit Distributed AI Research Institute, explained that one regulatory problem with the metaphor is that today's advanced models involve a complex infrastructure of distributed technologies beyond the control of a single kill switch. Eryk Salvaggio, a digital humanities researcher at the University of Cambridge, argued that the black box of AI cultivates useful confusion about what can and cannot be known about the complexity of frontier models. In proposing his since-failed AI Emergency Button Act bill, Sen. John Kennedy compared the concept to kill switches in machines such as jet skis. The articles also cite cognitive linguist George Lakoff and philosopher Mark Johnson, who described structural metaphors as relying on simple physical concepts and hiding some aspects of a concept by focusing attention on others.

The articles say the kill switch metaphor is rooted in the same rhetoric as the black box metaphor, and both blur the complex aspects of AI. The kill switch metaphor is ill-suited to regulating AI because there is no way to switch off an AI model without accounting for its distributed infrastructure and human influence, and there is no big red button, emergency brake or glass box hiding a lever. The articles say effective national regulation of AI will not begin with any single switch or any one person's finger. The articles do not say what happens next beyond noting that no national regulation with a kill switch exists to date.

stories.Headline: Dow Jones Futures: AMD, Nvidia Lead AI Trade Higher; Meta, Netflix, SpaceX, Tesla Earnings On Deck
stories.Summary:
SpaceX and Tesla have begun formal discussions about a possible merger, Elon Musk confirmed on October 21, 2026. Committees of independent directors at both companies were formed at shareholders’ request, and Musk said he is not taking part because of his conflict of interest. A person familiar with the matter said the talks began in recent weeks and could result in SpaceX acquiring Tesla, with Tesla working with an investment bank for advice. Musk called a combination “a good idea,” pointing to shared work in AI software, chip design, robotics and connectivity, but he cautioned that no agreement has been reached.

SpaceX reported third quarter revenue of $14.58 billion, up 161 percent from a year earlier, and net income of $4.4 billion, reversing a loss of $1.1 billion. AI revenue surged nearly tenfold to $7.56 billion, largely from renting computing capacity to developers including Anthropic, Alphabet and Reflection AI. Capital expenditure nearly tripled to $19.6 billion, and Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen said fourth quarter spending is expected to be between $35 billion and $40 billion. Starlink had 13.6 million subscribers, above the forecast of 12.19 million, while monthly revenue per subscriber fell to $69 from $99 in 2023. Musk also said the Terafab chip venture is expected to produce its first test chip around May or June next year, with volume production targeted for the third quarter of 2028.

Barclays suggested last week that a merger announcement could come before Tesla’s annual meeting on December 3. In an all stock deal, Barclays estimates Musk would hold about 37 percent of the equity and 56 percent of the votes. Shawn Campbell, an adviser at Camelthorn Investments, said investors are focused on Starlink revenue growth and improvement in Tesla’s auto margins. Bill Birmingham, head of research at REX Financial, said Tesla’s unveiling of a new Roadster with rocket technology on Thursday was a subtle argument for a merger ahead of the shareholder meeting.

Tesla is expected to report adjusted earnings of roughly 43 cents a share on revenue of about $27.88 billion, compared with 50 cents a year earlier. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, beating estimates, and has said capital spending will exceed $25 billion this year. Analysts expect negative free cash flow of $4.92 billion for the third quarter. SpaceX reports results on Tuesday and Tesla on Wednesday after markets close. Evercore ISI expects SpaceX to exit 2026 at an annualized revenue run rate of about $104 billion, with capital spending reaching about $151 billion in 2027.

stories.Headline: NVIDIA and Supply Chain Partners Expand Capacity to Accelerate AI Infrastructure Buildout
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA announced on October 21, 2026, at GTC Berlin, that it is working with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity for its accelerated computing and AI factory platform. The partners are Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and Unimicron Technology Corporation. The work covers substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines. NVIDIA said the aim is to strengthen the resiliency and redundancy of its global supply chain.

The agreements will drive a 2.5x increase in substrate capacity over the next three years. IBIDEN's Ono Plant in Japan, backed by a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance signed earlier in 2026, targets 3x current capacity, with more capacity ramping in the first quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics joins the substrate supply chain with existing capacity in South Korea and upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan. Unimicron's KF substrate expansion in Taiwan is expected to add capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028. Amkor plans to increase interposer wafer capacity in South Korea by more than 300% by the end of 2028.

NVIDIA expects total semiconductor testing capacity to double from calendar 2026 to 2027, with buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan and Singapore. A $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC will support new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027, and expanded testing in Singapore is expected to begin high-volume production in February 2027. SPIL is targeting a 15x increase in optical-engine capacity for co-packaged optics by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. Jensen Huang, NVIDIA's founder and CEO, said demand is extraordinary and capacity is the constraint, and he thanked the partners for expanding around the globe.

Separately, NVIDIA announced at GTC Berlin that European automakers and mobility providers, including Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride, are showcasing autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform. The demonstrations cover potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles and future robotaxi fleets, and Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and the NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for safe automated driving. NVIDIA introduced Halos SAFE, a framework within its Halos safety system that combines simulation and physical testing to help developers generate measurable, traceable safety evidence. It also announced Alpamayo 2 Edge, Alpamayo Agentic Factory and new Cosmos 3 Nano model variants to help developers build, customize and evaluate autonomous driving across vehicles, conditions and regions.

stories.Headline: Authors Bring Copyright Suits Targeting Meta's AI Training
stories.Summary:
Meta Platforms Inc. was hit with hundreds of new copyright complaints on Monday, October 19, 2026, from authors who say the company used their books to train its large language models without permission. Around 300 authors signed on to pursue individual claims, according to their attorneys at Freedman Normand Friedland LLP and Stris & Maher LLP. The lawsuits were filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California in San Francisco. The authors range from fiction novelists to journalists. The new cases depart from earlier AI copyright litigation that relied on the class action mechanism, where thousands of authors can be grouped into one case and litigate as a single unit.

The two law firms said they plan to file individual lawsuits against Meta for close to 1,000 additional authors in the coming months. Each author seeks statutory damages, which can reach a maximum of $150,000 per infringing work. The suits make claims similar to existing cases, alleging Meta downloaded hundreds of thousands of e-books from illegal online databases known as shadow libraries and used them to train its AI models. Meta did not immediately return a request for comment. AI companies including Meta have argued that their conduct falls under copyright law's fair use defense because they transform the copies into an entirely new technology.

The named cases include Reno v. Meta Platforms Inc., No. 3:26-cv-12131, Sheard v. Meta Platforms Inc., No. 3:26-cv-12126, Winspear v. Meta Platforms Inc., No. 3:26-cv-12100, and Older v. Meta Platforms Inc., No. 3:26-cv-12115, all dated 10/19/26.

Earlier copyright class actions against AI companies have drawn mixed results in the courts. The first class action involving authors against Anthropic PBC ended in a $1.5 billion settlement that would yield roughly $3,000 to each author who opted into the class. In another proposed class action, Kadrey v. Meta, the judge found the plaintiffs had failed to provide evidence that Meta's AI model was harming the market for their works.

stories.Headline: 3,000 year-long internships to be offered to tertiary students as AI reshapes entry-level jobs - CNA
stories.Summary:
About 3,000 year-long internships will be offered to tertiary students over the next three years, Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information Tan Kiat How announced on Oct 19, 2026, at the Singapore Computer Society's TechConnect event. The internships are part of Bridge2Tech, a set of expanded initiatives under the Infocomm Media Development Authority's TIP Alliance+, which now includes students from autonomous universities. Year-long internships have been offered to eligible Information and Digital Technologies students from the Institute of Technical Education and polytechnics since 2022. The event was held at the Singapore Institute of Technology campus in Punggol, before a hall of nearly 500 students and company leaders.

The 10- to 12-month internships will be integrated into students' curricula and jointly designed by educational institutions and employers, with IMDA providing funding support. IMDA will co-fund hiring costs, with firms receiving up to $1,000 monthly per intern for each eligible year-long internship. Eligible students can also receive IMDA funding of up to 90 per cent for approved courses and certifications in AI, cloud and cybersecurity, subject to applicable caps. A new Government Tech Domain Pathway will open for applications in November, and the government is working with partners on a HealthTech pathway for 2027. More than 200 employers have pledged support for skills-based hiring under TIP Alliance+, including DBS, Google, HSBC and Singtel.

Mr Tan said concerns among fresh graduates about their employment prospects are real and should not be dismissed or met with easy reassurance. He noted that AI can now assist with tasks junior engineers used to learn from, such as writing simpler programmes, debugging code, testing applications or maintaining systems, and described this as the disappearing early rungs of the career ladder. He said employers still need experienced engineers, but those engineers need to begin somewhere, and fresh graduates cannot be expected to arrive with years of practical experience or simply be told to learn more AI. He said new bridges between school and work must be built, and that this is a shared responsibility among educational institutions, employers, industry associations and the government. He also urged employers to recognise skills and practical experience, saying a diploma or degree remains valuable but qualifications alone cannot tell an employer everything about a person's potential.

Mr Tan echoed concerns raised by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong earlier in October that the bottom rung of career ladders might be broken because of AI adoption. Mr Tan said internships should not become an arms race to fill a resume, citing an internal National University of Singapore study that accumulating more internships eventually produces diminishing returns. He said IMDA will monitor the outcomes of the year-long internships closely and assess expansion of successful methods over time. The internships will span industries such as tech, finance and healthcare, and companies involved in previous runs include OCBC Bank, Accenture and PSA. Polytechnic graduate Pei Joon Yi, 20, who completed an internship at NTU's Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine building AI applications, said the year gave him room to build on what he had learnt and become more independent in approaching new projects.

stories.Headline: How AI is Changing the Work Behind the Work
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence has moved from a futuristic idea into everyday life, and people now meet it through voice assistants, personalized recommendations, search tools, and software that handles repetitive tasks. Businesses are adopting AI to improve efficiency, analyze information, and create new products and services. Modern AI includes machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, generative AI, and increasingly capable AI agents. IBM describes business AI as a way to automate work, optimize operations, support decisions, and create business value. Generative AI has made the technology more accessible because employees can interact with many systems using ordinary language instead of specialist programming knowledge.

AI is changing business by reducing repetitive work in areas such as customer service, marketing, forecasting, cybersecurity, software development, document processing, and internal knowledge management. Deloitte’s 2026 research found that productivity and efficiency remain among the most commonly reported benefits of enterprise AI adoption. A major development is the emergence of AI agents, which can interpret a broader goal, plan multiple steps, and carry out actions with varying levels of human supervision. Google Cloud has identified AI agents and agentic workflows as major trends in business technology, particularly for automating complex, multi-step processes. Microsoft’s 2026 Work Trend Index describes a shift in which AI and agents increasingly take on execution while people retain greater responsibility for directing work, making decisions, and owning outcomes.

City & State has also responded to AI use by elected officials, and its workflow now includes running written submissions through Pangram to detect AI content. Managing Editor Eric Holmberg wrote on October 20, 2026, that the ubiquity of AI usage by elected officials was a wake-up call. City Hall reporter Shenal Tissera recently emailed 29 City Council members’ offices to ask about affordable housing development, and he received seven responses that Pangram said likely included AI-generated text. Holmberg said it is disappointing that elected officials are relying on AI for public communications, and he argued that New Yorkers voted for them because of their lived experience and positions, not Claude’s. City & State is committed to using AI detection software for the long haul, and it may send fewer emails and make more phone calls.

The rise of AI does not mean human skills are becoming irrelevant, and the value of critical thinking, communication, creativity, leadership, and problem-solving may actually increase. AI can produce an answer quickly, but people still need to determine whether that answer makes sense, because a generated report may contain an inaccurate assumption or an automated recommendation may overlook an important business consideration. Privacy, cybersecurity, misinformation, bias, intellectual property, and inaccurate AI-generated information are among the issues organizations must consider. Recent research from the International Labour Organization highlights a gap between productivity improvements observed at individual task levels and the broader economic impact of AI adoption. Organizations that want to benefit should begin with practical problems, provide employee training, and establish human oversight for high-impact decisions in financial, legal, medical, or security contexts.

stories.Headline: SpaceX’s AI business is beating expectations
stories.Summary:
SpaceX reported third quarter revenue of $14.6 billion on Tuesday, a 161 percent increase from the same period a year earlier. The company earned $4.40 billion in net income, turning around from a loss of $1.05 billion a year ago. Its artificial intelligence business, renamed Super Intelligence, generated $7.5 billion in revenue and $431 million in profit. That profit would have been higher without $1.2 billion in one time stock based compensation expenses tied to the Cursor acquisition. The AI unit includes the Cursor coding tool, the Grok bot, and a neocloud business with 1.7 gigawatts of compute.

The results show AI now makes up 52 percent of SpaceX income. The connectivity segment, which includes Starlink, reported $5.2 billion in revenue, up 69 percent from a year earlier, and Starlink reached 13.6 million consumers. Total capital expenditures were $19.6 billion, and Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen said the company would spend $35 billion to $40 billion on new capital investments in the fourth quarter. Johnsen forecast total revenue for the first quarter of 2027 in the range of $33 billion to $37 billion. SpaceX still had a net income loss of $413 million in the first nine months of the year.

Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said he was spending four days a week in Memphis, Tennessee, at the Colossus II data center site. He said the constraint on deploying super intelligence is more in power, cooling, and infrastructure than in chips, and he compared SpaceX engineers to the New York Yankees playing in Little League. Musk said turbine makers face 12 to 18 month delays for metal blades and vanes, so SpaceX is using its metal casting capabilities to make those parts. He also said the next Starship test flight, expected in November, would attempt to recover both the first stage booster and the second stage.

SpaceX shares jumped nearly 4 percent in after hours trading to about $153.30, and the company has a valuation of nearly $1.95 trillion. This was the company’s second ever quarterly financial disclosure since it went public in June. Musk predicted SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 will be somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion. The earnings release came a day after Musk vowed to give one SpaceX share to every child in the United States next year, a pledge that could total nearly $11 billion based on about 73 million people under age 18.

Articles.Title: SpaceX’s AI business is beating expectations

stories.Headline: Anthropic, Google, ByteDance & Tencent Join the Fray: Why Tech Giants Are Collectively Flocking to AI-Powered Drug Discovery
stories.Summary:
Anthropic, Google, ByteDance and Tencent have all moved into AI-powered drug discovery, according to a 36Kr report published on October 20, 2026. Anthropic has started building physical wet labs and is recruiting biochemistry talent. Google's Isomorphic Labs keeps upgrading the AlphaFold protein structure prediction model, and its latest valuation reached 40 to 50 billion US dollars. ByteDance spun off its AI pharmaceutical company Anew Labs, which raised 290 million US dollars in a first round at a post-investment valuation of about 1.5 billion US dollars.

The article says AI compresses drug discovery time by 30 to 50 percent, and that AI-discovered molecules reach 80 to 90 percent success in Phase I trials against a historical average of 52 percent. More than 170 AI drug projects worldwide have entered clinical stages, and 7 AI drugs have entered or completed Phase III trials. Isomorphic Labs' IsoDDE engine is said to cut a search of 10^60 chemical spaces from several years to several days. Insilico Medicine's Rentosertib, found with AI help, has entered Phase III trials for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, predicted that AI could overcome most serious diseases in the next 5 to 10 years. Demis Hassabis of Google DeepMind has said the best use of AI is to improve human health, and he shared half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold. The US FDA said digital transformation will not change existing CGMP requirements and that quality oversight cannot be transferred because of AI. No AI drug has yet passed regulatory approval and reached the market.

The 36Kr article notes that AI mainly changes the upstream discovery stage, which accounts for only 38 percent of costs, while 62 percent goes to clinical trials and approval. It names high-quality data as the biggest bottleneck, since failed molecule data held by drug companies and CROs is rarely made public. Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta plan to invest 1.8 billion US dollars in a next-generation biological AI model and open data infrastructure. A separate Yahoo Finance article says Tencent joined ByteDance and Alibaba in placing large 2026 orders for Nvidia high-end AI chips, with combined orders exceeding Nvidia's planned output.

stories.Headline: How the Mississippi AG Cyber Crime Lab is used to track evidence, AI - The Clarion-Ledger
stories.Summary:
Attorney General Lynn Fitch opened the Mississippi Attorney General's Office Cyber Crime Lab to reporters on Oct. 20, 2026, for a tour of the digital forensics unit in Jackson. The Cyber Crime Division, established in 2000, investigates cyberattacks and helps law enforcement agencies collect digital evidence, and it also manages the Mississippi Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force and the Mississippi Cyber Fraud Task Force, a partnership with the United States Secret Service. The tour covered cryptocurrency, business email compromise, ATM jackpotting, skimmers, SMS phishing, artificial intelligence and CyberTips. It also included a demonstration of TracE, the office's electronic storage device K9 used to sniff out hidden digital evidence.

The lab supports local, federal and state agencies that lack the specialized tools to track advanced digital footprints, said Shawn Wolfe, director of the Cyber Crime Division. Forensic examiner Jamie White said the division uses commercial equipment such as Cellebrite and GrayKey to unlock phones and extract photos, texts, location history, encrypted messages and apps, and it has built in-house programs to fight ATM jackpotting and contraband devices in correctional facilities. White demonstrated a custom device that cracks a locked computer in about 45 seconds. The office has seized about 50 card skimmers in recent years, and Fitch said a single skimmer can facilitate up to $1 million in fraud. The crimes against children task force includes nearly 90 law enforcement agencies and 145 personnel, and its work includes Operation Muddy Waters, a two-week operation that led to nearly 70 arrests statewide.

Fitch called the division a national-level, top-notch team that is always working on initiatives to create solutions through partnerships. Nick Sprowles, an investigator with the Cyber Fraud Task Force, said investigators can preserve evidence, prosecute cases and put bad guys in jail. Charlie Rubisoff, deputy director of the Cyber Crime Division, said artificial intelligence is being used more and more by criminals and the landscape is changing almost daily. He pointed to research from the Tech Transparency Project showing an influx of apps that create non-consensual nude images, including of children, and said the division is working to control the spread of that material. Rubisoff said technology alone cannot solve the problem and called it a community effort, urging families to monitor children's devices responsibly.

stories.Headline: Toku launches Makimoto Flows, a visual builder for speech AI pipelines, taking its open-source initiative beyond transcription
stories.Summary:
Toku Ltd., a Singapore-headquartered AI customer experience platform listed on SGX, launched Makimoto Flows on 21 October 2026. Flows is a visual builder inside the company's open-source conversational AI initiative, and it lets developers assemble speech AI pipelines block by block and test each stage on a recorded call. The tool is live at makimoto.ai. On the canvas, developers connect blocks and test each step on its own. The Transcribe block turns audio into text using Kawa, the Summarise block generates a topic and short summary from the transcript, and the Tags block sorts each call into seven categories, including customer sentiment.

Every block runs in Singapore, so audio, transcripts and analysis stay in the country. A Chained Analysis starter template links the blocks in one click, and developers can change any block and rerun it to compare results. Each block maps to a Makimoto API endpoint, and any flow can be exported as ready-to-run Python code for uses such as call recaps and call triage. Thomas Laboulle, founder and CEO at Toku, said developers should control how their voice AI works, from the models they use to the way each stage connects. He said Flows puts the orchestration layer in front of them, so they can build a pipeline, run a recorded call through it and see what each step produces before anything reaches customers.

He added that models will keep changing, and the ability to compose them and know where they run is what lasts. Flows builds on the composable architecture Toku set out when it introduced Makimoto in April 2026 and takes the initiative beyond transcription. Kawa was released on schedule on 1 July 2026 and set up the transcription layer through a Singapore-hosted API, and summarisation and tagging endpoints followed in September. Next, Makimoto plans to add audio preparation blocks, starting with noise filtering. Developers can create a free account at makimoto.ai, and each account includes 1,000 free minutes.

stories.Headline: Inception Releases Mercury 3 Diffusion LLM at 1,068 Tokens per Second
stories.Summary:
Inception released Mercury 3 on Monday, October 20, 2026, according to the articles. It is the company's fourth Mercury model, following Mercury 1, Mercury 2 and Mercury 2.5. Mercury 1 launched in 2025, and Mercury 2.5 added tunable reasoning and a 260K context window. Mercury 3 is a diffusion LLM that writes answers in parallel rather than token by token. Inception reports 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs and a 1M-token context window.

The model is API only, with no open weights or quantized builds, and Inception did not disclose its parameter count. Inception says it is more than 40x larger than Mercury 1, and average quality rose about 3x between the two models. On Inception's own benchmark table, Mercury 3 leads GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on 8 of 12 tests, including SWE-Bench Atlas at 51.08 and IFBench at 76.84. It trails on DeepSWE v1 at 46.31 and MRCR v2 at 75.50. Launch pricing is $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.35 per million output tokens, which is 50% off the eventual standard price of $0.20 and $0.70.

CEO Stefano Ermon told The Deep View that Mercury 3 is the most capable diffusion-based language model on the market. He said it is comparable to the Luna and Haiku models but way faster, at 1,000 tokens per second, and almost instant. Ermon also said the company is working on developments that could make the launch price permanent in the weeks ahead. Inception reported that swarms of Mercury 3 agents used for recursive self improvement raised overall speed by 16% on top of its own upgrades.

The articles say diffusion models start from a rough draft of the full answer and refine every position over a few passes in parallel, which means fewer sequential steps and faster output on the same GPUs. Inception's early-access partners include TinyFish, which ran 50 live Mind2Web web-navigation tasks, and Octen AI, which reported 0.9 seconds median generation. The Deep View notes that Google DeepMind released DiffusionGemma in June with 26 billion parameters. It says the open question is whether diffusion LLMs remain a niche for real-time applications or become a long-term challenger to frontier models.

stories.Headline: Your Car Comes to You, and AI Understands You: OMODA & JAECOO's Super Intelligent Experience Lab Is About to Begin
stories.Summary:
OMODA & JAECOO held its Super Intelligent Experience Lab from October 19 to 21, 2026, in Wuhu, China, as part of its "DRIVE TO THE NEXT VIBE" International User Summit. The event brought together global media and guests to test two technologies, SIVP (Super Intelligent Valet Parking) and SIAS (Super Intelligent AI Space). SIVP was demonstrated through remote vehicle summoning, parking in complex spaces and obstacle avoidance. The company said the event recreated real driving and parking scenarios to show vehicles perceiving their surroundings and making rapid decisions.

SIVP is an assisted driving feature and does not replace the driver, according to the company. Before activating it, the network connection must be stable and the vehicle must be in a parking area separated from public roads. SIAS focuses on four capabilities: better intent understanding, better understanding of user habits, better understanding of emotions and better understanding of trends. The event included challenges such as responding to multiple requests in one sentence, understanding intentions behind users' words, giving personalized recommendations and enabling interactions with AI virtual pets. The company says the brand has sold one million vehicles in three years and has expanded into 79 markets, including 22 European countries.

The content was provided by OMODA & JAECOO, and the article lists Sonny as the contact person. The company describes itself as a youthful, personalized global brand with a vision of "Co-creating a Beautiful Life with Young People." It says OMODA aims to be "the World's Leading Crossover Brand" and JAECOO a "Global Elegant Off-Road Brand." It also says it works with AiMOGA on robots and uses SHS super hybrid technology covering PHEV and HEV, while accelerating BEV deployment.

A separate Ipsos survey released on October 20, 2026, looked at Americans' awareness of Artificial Intelligence and Super Intelligence. It found that 49% said they had heard a great deal or quite a bit about AI, compared with 13% for SI. Among those familiar with the terms, 65% were at least somewhat confident in their understanding of AI, versus 51% for SI. The poll was conducted October 9 to 11, 2026, with 1,016 adults aged 18 or older, and had a margin of sampling error of plus or minus 3.2 percentage points.

stories.Headline: Apple to make Siri AI available in S. Korea this month: sources - Yonhap News Agency
stories.Summary:
Apple will make its generative AI-powered Siri assistant available in Korean this month, industry sources said on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. The move follows a beta launch of the new Siri in English in September. Korean customers will soon be able to use the assistant, according to the sources. The company described Siri AI as a more capable and conversational assistant.

The service understands personal context, has broad world knowledge, is aware of what is on screen, and can take more actions across apps, Apple said in a release. For example, if a user asks about a recipe for a dish eaten on a previous trip, Siri can search the user's message logs and pull up a link to that recipe. Its visual intelligence offers image understanding and multimodal capabilities, letting users ask about visual content across iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro. Siri AI is powered by Google's Gemini, but Apple said it operates within its own security framework and is designed to immediately delete data for answers that need AI processing.

Apple is said to have expanded integration with domestic apps and is reportedly working with local IT companies, including Kakao Corp. and Naver Corp., to optimize the service. Apple is the company behind the service, and it said Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant. The company said the assistant operates within its own security framework and deletes data immediately when AI processing is required. Apple also said the assistant can understand personal context and take systemwide app actions.

The sources who spoke to Yonhap provided the timing of the Korean launch. The expansion comes after the English beta launch in September. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the expected launch this month. They also do not give a specific date for the Korean service.

Articles.Title: Apple to make Siri AI available in S. Korea this month: sources - Yonhap News Agency

stories.Headline: Nvidia, German government team to advance industrial AI
stories.Summary:
At the Invest in Germany summit in Berlin on 20 October 2026, Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang revealed a joint initiative to advance edge AI models for physical AI. The declaration sets out an agreement for the German federal government to work with Nvidia to formalise and expand Nvidia's collaboration with Germany and its Industry 4.0 platform. Merz said his government aims to make Germany one of the most advanced places in the world, not just in the European Union, to work with AI and integrate it into industry. Huang said Nvidia's relationship with German industry began in the early 2000s by supplying technology for gaming systems, workstations and automotive design, and has evolved to partnerships in autonomous vehicle development and digital twins for manufacturing.

According to media reports first cited by Handelsblatt, the federal government plans to contribute a nine-figure sum to the partnership. Around a dozen German companies are expected to join the government-backed project, including Siemens, Audi and AI start-up Black Forest Labs from Freiburg im Breisgau. Nvidia said it invested almost one billion dollars in Germany in 2025 and holds stakes in numerous German start-ups and established firms. At the summit, Amazon also announced plans to invest around 16 billion euros in Germany in 2027, with one third, or 4.8 billion euros, going mainly to the Frankfurt am Main region to expand data centres for its cloud provider AWS. Amazon said around 3,000 employees already work for AWS in Germany.

Merz called on companies in Germany to open their industrial data for artificial intelligence to safeguard the competitiveness of sectors such as the car industry, arguing that preserving Germany's industrial base is a crucial advantage over other economies. He said Germany's biggest advantage is its Mittelstand, small and medium businesses, and urged them to open their doors for AI to make use of their data. Huang said national expertise and knowledge set the German economy apart and that AI will only amplify it, adding that AI can augment capability but will not replace it. Huang also said it pained him to see how far Germany had fallen behind, and advised the country to simply get to work.

Nvidia announced AI solutions at Siemens' Erlangen factory that cut production engineering effort by up to 85% and manufacturing costs by up to 20%, and an expanded partnership with Mercedes-Benz to co-develop next-generation automated driving systems using Nvidia's Hyperion, Alpamayo and Halos technologies alongside Mercedes-Benz's MB.OS platform. Nvidia is also using Jupiter, Europe's first exascale supercomputer at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre, to run a 104-qubit fault-tolerant quantum computing simulation that validates a magic state cultivation approach, claimed to require 90% fewer qubits than previous methods. Nvidia announced planned investments in four German startups in physical AI: Agile Robots, Avelios Medical, Mirelo and Reflex Aerospace. The International Monetary Fund now expects growth of 1.3 percent in Germany in 2026, after previously forecasting only 0.7 percent, and whether further upswing materialises thanks to investment by US tech giants remains to be seen.

stories.Headline: Delinea Fastpath Launches MCP Server for AI-Powered Access Governance and Audit Readiness
stories.Summary:
Delinea announced on October 21, 2026 that it had launched the Delinea Fastpath MCP Server, a new capability that connects access governance data to the AI assistants teams already use. The company said the tool uses the Model Context Protocol so finance, IT, audit and compliance teams can ask natural-language questions and get fine-grained, cross-application answers on access risk, access reviews and audit readiness, with remediation options in seconds. Delinea said the launch responds to a problem in which complex ERP security models surface thousands of segregation of duties conflicts, leaving finance teams unsure where to start and slowing remediation and audit preparation. The announcement was made in San Francisco.

The company said the server lets teams query live Fastpath data in plain language, highlights the most material risks and cuts audit preparation time, and requires no data migration because every answer reflects the customer's environment as it is at that moment. Delinea said teams can ask about users, roles, access risk, controls and access reviews across more than 100 connected cloud and on-premises applications at once, including Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Oracle, SAP, Salesforce and Workday. It said more than thirty out-of-the-box native connections surface risk down to the lowest securable object, using rulesets built by audit experts for each application's security model and based on the COSO framework and ISACA remediation best practices. Fastpath is independently audited under SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2, and the company said every answer runs in that same audited environment and returns the same governed data. The capability is read-only and bound to each user's permissions, so a connected AI assistant cannot change anything in Fastpath.

Jason Mitchell, Executive Vice President of Product and Technology at Delinea, said customers spend too much of their time turning access data into decisions and that the server gives that time back. He said finance teams and business application owners can ask a question in their own words and get a clear, prioritized answer they can act on, grounded in the same data their auditors already rely on. Neil Poynton, Director of ERP at Chromalox, said getting answers out of access data used to mean building Excel lookups and stitching data points together by hand, and that with the server the company will be able to ask a question in plain language and pull together information held in Delinea Fastpath in a fraction of the time. He called it an exciting addition to the company's solution. Delinea said more than 9,000 organizations, including two-thirds of the Fortune 100, rely on it.

Delinea described Fastpath as a leader in application access governance that helps organizations automate governance of human and agentic access across business applications to maintain continuous audit readiness. It said Fastpath automates key IT general controls, including segregation of duties risk analysis, to help organizations reduce risk, simplify compliance and strengthen oversight of sensitive applications and data. Delinea described itself as an identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long, extending privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action through just-in-time authorization. The company invited readers to visit its website to see a demo of the Fastpath MCP Server and learn more.
